items.title: Over a flat neighbourhood covering the I-power torsion modules on both sides are equivalent and Hom does not change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a flat ring map R -> S and a finitely generated ideal I with R/I -> S/IS an isomorphism, and asserts three things: that the natural map on I-power torsion submodules is an isomorphism; that Hom_R(M, N) -> Hom_S(M tensor_R S, N tensor_R S) is an isomorphism whenever either M or N is I-power torsion; and that base change is an equivalence between I-power torsion modules and IS-power torsion modules (source lines 24300-24318). The proof gives each part. Part (1) sets M' = M/M[I^∞] and uses the exact sequence 0 -> M[I^∞] -> M -> M' -> 0 together with M[I^∞] = M[I^∞] tensor_R S to reduce to showing (M' tensor_R S)[(IS)^∞] = 0; writing I = (f_1, ..., f_t), it uses the divide-by-torsion lemma to get M'[I^∞] = 0, so the map x -> (f_1^n x, ..., f_t^n x) into the direct sum of t copies of M' is injective for every n > 0, and flatness of S keeps it injective after base change, giving (M' tensor_R S)[I^n] = 0 as required (proof lines 24325-24342). Part (2) splits into two cases: if N is I-power torsion then N tensor_R S = N and the map is an isomorphism by the adjoint tensor-restrict lemma; if M is I-power torsion then any map M -> N lands in N[I^∞] and any map after base change lands in (N tensor_R S)[(IS)^∞], so part (1) lets one replace N by N[I^∞] and reduce to the previous case (proof lines 24345-24354). Part (3) argues that the functor is fully faithful by (2) and checks essential surjectivity for IS-power torsion modules (proof lines 24357-24358 and following). The non-routine steps are the injection-into-a-direct-sum argument in part (1) and the reduction of part (2) to the case already handled.
